summary: Fourteen capabilities follow the flow of goods (plan, store, move, ship, clear) and then the modes that carry goods and people (road fleets, air, sea, rail, transit, travel distribution, road networks). SCOR's plan and deliver processes and APQC category 4 drove the goods side; GS1's identify-capture-share families shaped identification and traceability; ICAO's Doc 9854 concept components, IMO e-navigation, railML and AAR, Transmodel and GTFS, and ARC-IT with the Highway Capacity Manual shaped the mode-specific capabilities. Routing and scheduling leaves are named for the public instance sets that test them.

capabilities.name: Supply chain planning
capabilities.definition: Given demand history, the network of sites and lanes, lead times and costs, decide how much to stock, make and move where and when, and where facilities should be.

crosswalk.label: Plan for and align supply chain resources

onet_categories: Materials requirements planning logistics and supply chain software
capabilities.notes: Was seed 'Supply chain and demand planning, inventory optimization'. Shop-floor MRP and finite-capacity scheduling are handed to produce; the solvers to science. Spare-parts provisioning added because the military logistics products in O*NET (SYSPARS, Spare Cost) do exactly this.

tasks.name: Demand forecasting for replenishment
tasks.definition: Given sales or shipment history by item and location with calendar and promotion data, produce forecasts at the levels planners use.
tasks.inputs: item-location demand history, hierarchy, calendar, prices and promotions
tasks.outputs: point and quantile forecasts by item, location and period

crosswalk.label: Identify, Prioritize and Aggregate Supply Chain Requirements

tasks.benchmarkable: yes: the M5 competition (Walmart hierarchical unit sales) has public data and scoring
tasks.notes: Generic time-series methods belong to science; this task is the planning application with item-location hierarchies.

tasks.name: Multi-site supply planning
tasks.definition: Given net demand, sourcing rules, site capacities and lead times across a network, decide production, transfer and purchase quantities by period.
tasks.inputs: demand plan, bills of distribution, capacities, lead times, costs
tasks.outputs: time-phased supply plan by site and lane; capacity and shortage exceptions
onet_products: Oracle PeopleSoft Enterprise Supply Planning Multi-Site Material Planner
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: formulations are standard linear and mixed-integer programs, but there is no shared instance set
tasks.notes: Single-plant MRP explosion stays with produce.

tasks.name: Inventory policy optimization
tasks.definition: Given demand distributions, lead times, costs and service targets for one or many echelons, set safety stocks, reorder points and order quantities.
tasks.inputs: demand and lead-time distributions, holding and shortage costs, network structure, service targets
tasks.outputs: safety stock, reorder point and order-up-to levels by item and location; expected service and cost
state_of_art: SAP Integrated Business Planning for Inventory
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: Willems (2008) published 38 real multi-echelon supply chains for safety-stock placement, with reference solutions

tasks.name: Supply chain network design
tasks.definition: Given candidate facility sites, demand points, flows and costs, choose which facilities to open and how to assign flows to minimize cost under capacity limits.
tasks.inputs: customer demand, candidate sites and capacities, fixed and variable costs, transport costs
tasks.outputs: facilities to open, flow assignment, total cost and service levels
onet_products: Integrated Decision Support Corporation Netwise Supply Chain
Location allocation decision support system LADSS
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: OR-Library capacitated warehouse location instances (Beasley) and the Holmberg capacitated facility location set

capabilities.name: Warehouse and inventory control
capabilities.definition: Given stock, storage locations, orders and identification events, keep an accurate record of what is where and direct the work of storing, picking and packing it.
onet_categories: Materials requirements planning logistics and supply chain software
capabilities.notes: Was seed 'Warehouse management and inventory control; barcoding and labeling'. Kept as one capability; the GS1 identify-capture-share families became the identification and traceability tasks. Food, menu and kitchen inventory go to commerce; laboratory chemical inventory to science; forest inventory to earth.

tasks.name: Storage location assignment
tasks.definition: Given items, their demand and dimensions, and a warehouse layout, assign items to storage locations (slotting and putaway) to reduce travel and respect constraints.
tasks.inputs: SKU velocity and dimensions, location dimensions, layout, compatibility rules
tasks.outputs: item-to-location assignment; expected pick travel

crosswalk.label: Receive Product from Source or Make

tasks.benchmarkable: partly: slotting is a quadratic assignment problem with QAPLIB instances, but no warehouse-specific shared set

tasks.name: Order batching and picker routing
tasks.definition: Given open orders, item locations and the warehouse layout, group orders into pick batches or waves and sequence each picker's route.
tasks.inputs: order lines, item locations, aisle layout, picker and cart capacity
tasks.outputs: batches or waves, pick lists in route sequence, travel distance
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: picker routing in rectangular warehouses has exact algorithms (Ratliff and Rosenthal) and published batching instances, but no single standard set

tasks.name: Cartonization and pack planning
tasks.definition: Given the items of an order and the available box sizes, choose boxes and item placements that minimize shipped volume or cost.
tasks.inputs: item dimensions and weights, box catalogue, carrier dimensional-weight rules
tasks.outputs: boxes per order with item assignments and placements
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: three-dimensional bin packing instance classes of Martello, Pisinger and Vigo

tasks.name: Stock records and cycle counting
tasks.definition: Given receipts, issues, transfers and counts, maintain on-hand balances by item, lot and location, and schedule counts to find and correct discrepancies.
tasks.inputs: inventory transactions, count results, item and location master data
tasks.outputs: on-hand balances, custody history, count schedules and variance adjustments
tasks.benchmarkable: no: record keeping is transactional; correctness is a matter of tests, not a leaderboard
tasks.notes: Includes tool and equipment check-in and check-out.

tasks.name: Barcode and logistics label generation
tasks.definition: Given identifiers and shipment data, encode them in linear or two-dimensional symbols and lay out a compliant label for printing.
tasks.inputs: identifiers (item number, serial shipping container code, lot, dates), label template, printer
tasks.outputs: printable label with conformant barcode symbols
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: generated symbols can be graded against ISO/IEC 15415 and 15416 and GS1 application-identifier rules

tasks.name: Barcode decoding from images
tasks.definition: Given a camera or scanner image, locate and decode every linear and two-dimensional symbol in it.
tasks.inputs: image or scan line
tasks.outputs: decoded symbol data, symbology and position
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: public barcode image datasets (Muenster BarcodeDB, ArTe-Lab 1D barcode collections) give decode-rate benchmarks

tasks.name: RFID and identification event capture
tasks.definition: Given raw tag reads from readers and portals, filter and translate them into business events saying what was observed where, when and why.
tasks.inputs: raw tag reads, reader and location configuration, tag data encoding
tasks.outputs: standard visibility events (object, aggregation, transaction) in a repository
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: EPCIS conformance can be tested; read filtering lacks shared datasets

tasks.name: Lot traceability
tasks.definition: Given recorded transformation and shipment events, trace a lot forward to everyone who received it and backward to every input it came from.
tasks.inputs: lot-level receipt, transformation and shipment events
tasks.outputs: forward and backward trace graphs; recall lists
onet_products: AgInfoLink Meat Inventory Tracking System MITS
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: answers are exact given the events, so synthetic event sets can score completeness, but none are shared

capabilities.name: Freight transportation management
capabilities.definition: Given shipments to move, carriers, rates and equipment, decide how to consolidate, load, price, book and follow them to delivery.
onet_categories: Materials requirements planning logistics and supply chain software
capabilities.notes: Was seed 'Transportation management, freight rating and load planning'. Parcel and mail processing split into its own capability because rate-and-label shipping and postal presort are separate product families and functions.

tasks.name: Freight rating and carrier selection
tasks.definition: Given a shipment and carriers' contracts and tariffs, compute each carrier's charges with accessorials and choose the carrier and service.
tasks.inputs: origin, destination, freight class, weight, dimensions, service, tariffs and contracts
tasks.outputs: rated quotes by carrier and service; selected carrier
onet_products: Cadre Technologies Cadence Transportation Management System
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: rating is deterministic given tariffs, but tariffs are proprietary

tasks.name: Freight lane procurement
tasks.definition: Given lanes, volumes and carrier bids, including package bids, award lanes to carriers to minimize cost subject to capacity and business rules.
tasks.inputs: lane volumes, carrier bids and package bids, capacity and award rules
tasks.outputs: lane awards by carrier; expected cost
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: winner determination instances from the Combinatorial Auction Test Suite include a transport-like 'paths' distribution

tasks.name: Shipment consolidation and load building
tasks.definition: Given orders with dates, sizes and destinations, group them into truckloads, multi-stop loads or less-than-truckload shipments and choose the mode.
tasks.inputs: orders, ship windows, equipment, rates by mode
tasks.outputs: planned loads with stops and modes; cost
onet_products: Cadre Technologies Accuplus Integrated Distribution Logistics System
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: modeled as vehicle routing with split deliveries; no consolidation-specific instance set

tasks.name: Container and truck load planning
tasks.definition: Given cargo items and a container, trailer or aircraft hold, place the items in three dimensions to maximize utilization while meeting weight, axle, stacking and stability limits.
tasks.inputs: item dimensions, weights, orientations, stacking rules; container dimensions and weight limits
tasks.outputs: three-dimensional placement and load sequence; utilization and weight distribution

crosswalk.label: Load Vehicle and Generate Shipping Documents

tasks.benchmarkable: yes: Bischoff and Ratcliff container loading classes BR1 to BR15 in OR-Library

tasks.name: Pallet and case pattern design
tasks.definition: Given a case size and pallet, or a product and candidate cases, find stacking patterns that maximize cases per pallet within height and weight limits.
tasks.inputs: product or case dimensions, pallet size, height and weight limits
tasks.outputs: layer patterns and stack; cases per pallet
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: the manufacturer's pallet loading problem has standard Cover I and Cover II instance sets

tasks.name: Shipment tracking and arrival prediction
tasks.definition: Given carrier status messages, positions and proof-of-delivery records, keep each shipment's status current and predict its arrival time.
tasks.inputs: status messages, positions, schedules, delivery confirmations
tasks.outputs: shipment status, predicted arrival with uncertainty, exceptions

crosswalk.label: Receive and Verify Product by Customer

onet_products: Strategic Business Systems Proof of Delivery
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: arrival-time error can be scored on public vessel AIS and trip data, but no shared freight set

tasks.name: Freight forwarding and consolidation
tasks.definition: Given a customer's shipment, book multi-leg, multi-modal carriage, consolidate it into master shipments and produce house and master documents.
tasks.inputs: shipment details, routings, carrier schedules and space
tasks.outputs: bookings, house and master bills, consolidated manifests
tasks.benchmarkable: no: transactional workflow without an optimization or prediction target

capabilities.name: Parcel and mail processing
capabilities.definition: Given packages and mail pieces with addresses, validate the addresses, rate, label and presort the pieces, and read and sort them in the postal network.
onet_categories: Materials requirements planning logistics and supply chain software
Data base user interface and query software
capabilities.notes: New, not a seed: split from transportation management because parcel shipping and postal processing have their own products (carrier shipping clients, postage, presort, address recognition) and their own benchmarks.

tasks.name: Multi-carrier parcel rating and labeling
tasks.definition: Given a package and destination, rate it across parcel carriers and services, then produce the carrier label, manifest and tracking number.
tasks.inputs: package weight and dimensions, addresses, service requirements, carrier accounts
tasks.outputs: rates by carrier, chosen service, carrier label, manifest, tracking number
onet_products: Varsity ShipSoft Supply Chain Execution Suite
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: carrier rate tables are public, so rating is checkable, but label conformance is carrier-certified

tasks.name: Postal address validation
tasks.definition: Given a free-text or fielded address, parse and standardize it and match it to the postal authority's deliverable-address file.
tasks.inputs: address text or fields
tasks.outputs: standardized address, delivery point code, match confidence

crosswalk.label: S42: International postal address components and templates

tasks.benchmarkable: yes: USPS CASS certification test files have reference answers

tasks.name: Mail presort and postage calculation
tasks.definition: Given a mailing list and mail class, sort pieces into the trays, sacks and pallets the postal rules define and compute the discounted postage.
tasks.inputs: addresses, mail class and shape, postal sortation rules and rates
tasks.outputs: presorted list, container labels, postage statement
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: USPS PAVE certification checks presort output against rules, but test sets are not public

tasks.name: Address recognition and sortation
tasks.definition: Given images of mail pieces or parcels, read the destination address and barcode and assign each piece to a sort destination.
tasks.inputs: piece images, address directory, sort plan
tasks.outputs: recognized address, delivery point, sort bin
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: the CEDAR handwritten address database collected for USPS is a standard recognition benchmark

capabilities.name: Vehicle routing and scheduling
capabilities.definition: Given stops with demands and time constraints, vehicles and a travel-time network, plan the routes and schedules that serve the stops at least cost.
onet_categories: Materials requirements planning logistics and supply chain software
capabilities.notes: Was seed 'Vehicle routing, scheduling and dispatch'. Planned routing is kept here with tasks named for their standard instance sets; real-time dispatch moved to move.fleet_dispatch. General solvers go to science.

tasks.name: Capacitated vehicle routing
tasks.definition: Given a depot, customer demands, vehicle capacity and travel costs, find routes that serve every customer once at minimum total cost.
tasks.inputs: depot, customer locations and demands, vehicle capacity, distance matrix
tasks.outputs: routes and total cost
onet_products: UPS Logistics Technologies Roadnet Transportation Suite
Integrated Decision Support Corporation Route Advice
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: CVRPLIB, especially the Uchoa et al. X instances, and the Augerat A, B and P sets have best-known solutions

tasks.name: Vehicle routing with time windows
tasks.definition: Given customers with demands, service times and delivery windows, find capacity- and time-feasible routes minimizing vehicles and distance.
tasks.inputs: customers, demands, time windows, service times, fleet, travel times
tasks.outputs: routes with arrival times; vehicles used and distance
onet_products: UPS Logistics Technologies Roadnet Transportation Suite
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: Solomon's 56 instances and the Gehring and Homberger 200 to 1000 customer sets; the DIMACS 2021 challenge used them

tasks.name: Pickup and delivery routing
tasks.definition: Given paired pickup and delivery requests with time windows, build routes that visit each pickup before its delivery within capacity.
tasks.inputs: paired requests, time windows, loads, fleet, travel times
tasks.outputs: routes and schedules
onet_products: Integrated Decision Support Corporation Route Advice
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: Li and Lim pickup-and-delivery with time windows instances

tasks.name: Dial-a-ride passenger routing
tasks.definition: Given door-to-door passenger trip requests with time windows and maximum ride times, route and schedule shared vehicles.
tasks.inputs: trip requests, time windows, ride-time limits, vehicle capacity and depots
tasks.outputs: vehicle routes, pickup and drop-off times, ride times
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: Cordeau (2006) dial-a-ride instances

tasks.name: Capacitated arc routing
tasks.definition: Given a street network where streets rather than points need service, such as refuse collection, plowing or meter reading, find vehicle routes covering every required street.
tasks.inputs: street network, required edges with demands, vehicle capacity, depot
tasks.outputs: routes over the network and total deadhead and service cost
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: the gdb, val and egl capacitated arc routing instance sets

tasks.name: Multi-depot and periodic routing
tasks.definition: Given customers needing service on some days of a planning horizon from several depots, choose visit days, depot assignment and routes.
tasks.inputs: customers with visit frequencies and allowable patterns, depots, fleet, travel costs
tasks.outputs: visit calendar, depot assignment, daily routes
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: Cordeau, Gendreau and Laporte (1997) multi-depot and periodic routing instances

tasks.name: Driver-preferred route sequencing
tasks.definition: Given a route's stops and examples of how drivers actually sequenced past routes, produce the stop sequence a driver would follow.
tasks.inputs: stops with zones and time windows, travel times, historical driven sequences
tasks.outputs: stop sequence
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: the 2021 Amazon Last Mile Routing Research Challenge released routes and a scoring function

capabilities.name: Fleet dispatch and tracking
capabilities.definition: Given live requests, vehicle positions and driver status, assign work to vehicles as it arrives and keep track of where vehicles are and whether drivers are within their rules.
onet_categories: Materials requirements planning logistics and supply chain software
Data base user interface and query software
capabilities.notes: Merges seed 'Fleet tracking and telematics' with the dispatch part of 'Vehicle routing, scheduling and dispatch': real-time assignment depends on the tracking data and the products bundle them. Emergency computer-aided dispatch stays with govern; vehicle diagnostics with operate.

tasks.name: Taxi and ride-hail dispatch
tasks.definition: Given ride requests arriving in real time and the positions and states of vehicles, assign requests to vehicles and reposition idle ones.
tasks.inputs: request stream, vehicle positions and states, travel-time network
tasks.outputs: assignments, pickup estimates, repositioning moves
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: replay of public NYC taxi trip records is the common testbed, but simulators and scoring differ

tasks.name: Truckload load and driver assignment
tasks.definition: Given loads to cover and drivers and tractors with positions, hours and home domiciles, assign loads, swaps and relays to maximize coverage and profit.
tasks.inputs: load tenders, driver and tractor states, hours available, rates
tasks.outputs: load-driver assignments, relay and swap plans
onet_products: Integrated Decision Support Corporation Swap Advice
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: dynamic assignment models are well studied but there is no public instance set

tasks.name: Dynamic vehicle routing
tasks.definition: Given routes in progress and new requests revealed over the day, decide which requests to accept and how to re-plan routes in real time.
tasks.inputs: current routes and positions, request stream, time windows, travel times
tasks.outputs: updated routes and dispatch decisions at each epoch
onet_products: Computer aided dispatching auto routing software
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: the EURO Meets NeurIPS 2022 Vehicle Routing Competition dynamic track has instances and a simulator

tasks.name: Open-pit haul truck dispatch
tasks.definition: Given shovels, dumps, haul trucks and their positions and states, assign each truck its next destination to meet production and blend targets.
tasks.inputs: shovel and dump locations and rates, truck positions and states, haul road network, targets
tasks.outputs: truck assignments, shovel utilization and production
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: evaluated in discrete-event mine simulators without a shared benchmark
tasks.notes: Mine planning itself belongs to earth.

tasks.name: Vehicle tracking and map matching
tasks.definition: Given noisy positioning fixes from a vehicle, infer the road path driven, its timing and geofence entries and exits.
tasks.inputs: positioning fixes, road network, geofences
tasks.outputs: matched path, trip segments, stop and geofence events
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: the Newson and Krumm (2009) Seattle map-matching dataset with ground truth

tasks.name: Hours-of-service logging

tasks.inputs: duty-status events, engine and movement data, rule set
tasks.outputs: record of duty status, violations, available hours

crosswalk.label: Hours of service of drivers (Subpart B: Electronic Logging Devices)

onet_products: ddlsoftware.com drivers daily log program DDL
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: the rules are deterministic and FMCSA publishes electronic logging device test procedures

tasks.name: Driver behavior and fuel performance scoring
tasks.definition: Given vehicle data on speed, braking, idling and fuel use, score drivers and vehicles and flag unsafe or wasteful behavior.
tasks.inputs: vehicle bus and telematics data, trip context
tasks.outputs: per-driver and per-trip scores and events
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: public driving datasets exist but no agreed scoring target

tasks.name: Fuel purchase planning
tasks.definition: Given a planned truck route, fuel prices at stations along it and tank and network-discount rules, choose where and how much to buy.

tasks.outputs: fuel stops and quantities; total fuel cost
onet_products: Integrated Decision Support Corporation Expert Fuel
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: exact dynamic-programming solutions exist for the single-route case, but no public instances

capabilities.name: Trade compliance and shipping documents

onet_categories: Materials requirements planning logistics and supply chain software
Data base user interface and query software
capabilities.notes: Was seed 'Trade compliance, customs and shipping documentation'. Customs administration by the state (risk targeting, revenue) is govern's; this capability is the trader's and broker's side.

tasks.name: Tariff classification

tasks.name: Restricted party screening

tasks.outputs: candidate matches with scores
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: lists are public, but labeled match sets for scoring are not

tasks.name: Customs declaration filing

tasks.outputs: declaration messages, filing status, release
onet_products: Automated system for customs data ASYCUDA

tasks.name: Duty, landed cost and origin determination
tasks.definition: Given a classified product, its bill of materials and the trade lane, determine preferential origin eligibility and compute duties, taxes and landed cost.
tasks.inputs: tariff code, value, bill of materials with origins, trade agreement rules
tasks.outputs: origin determination, duty and tax amounts, landed cost

tasks.name: Dangerous goods classification and documentation

tasks.inputs: substance data, quantity, packaging, mode
tasks.outputs: UN number, class, packing group, label and placard requirements, shipping declaration

crosswalk.label: Recommendations on the Transport of Dangerous Goods

tasks.benchmarkable: partly: answers are determined by the regulations, so test cases can be built, but none are shared

tasks.name: Shipping document and message generation
tasks.definition: Given shipment data, produce bills of lading, commercial invoices, packing lists and the equivalent electronic messages.
tasks.inputs: shipment, parties, goods, terms
tasks.outputs: documents and electronic messages

crosswalk.label: UN Layout Key for trade documents

onet_products: Starre Enterprises Star Bill of Lading
tasks.benchmarkable: no: document assembly is deterministic

capabilities.name: Flight planning and airline operations
capabilities.definition: Given an aircraft, crew, payload, schedule and the weather and airspace, plan each flight and assign aircraft and crews to the schedule.

crosswalk.label: AOC air-ground data and message exchange

onet_categories: Data base user interface and query software

Drone survey mission planning goes to earth; flight simulators to learn; aircraft maintenance tracking to operate.

tasks.name: Flight route and fuel planning

tasks.name: Preflight briefing and notice filtering

tasks.benchmarkable: partly: route safety can be checked against public charts, but no scored route set exists

tasks.name: Ship weather routing
tasks.definition: Given departure, destination, the ship's speed and fuel response to waves and wind, and a forecast, find the route and speed profile minimizing time, fuel or risk.
tasks.inputs: forecast wind, waves and currents, ship performance model, constraints
tasks.outputs: route and speed schedule, predicted fuel and arrival time
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: open forecast archives allow comparison, but there is no reference instance set

tasks.name: Target tracking and collision avoidance
tasks.definition: Given radar, AIS and camera observations of nearby vessels and obstacles, track them, compute closest approach and propose rule-compliant maneuvers.
tasks.inputs: radar targets, AIS reports, camera images, own-ship state
tasks.outputs: tracked targets, closest point of approach and time, collision alarms and maneuver advice

crosswalk.label: International Regulations for Preventing Collisions at Sea (COLREGs)

tasks.benchmarkable: partly: public AIS archives and maritime obstacle datasets (Singapore Maritime Dataset, MODS) score detection but not maneuver decisions

tasks.name: Voyage logbooks and reporting
tasks.definition: Given bridge and engine events, keep the official deck and engine logs and produce required voyage, emission and weather reports.
tasks.inputs: navigation events, engine data, observations
tasks.outputs: logbook entries and voyage reports
tasks.benchmarkable: no: record keeping

tasks.name: Ship routing and cargo scheduling
tasks.definition: Given cargoes with pickup and delivery ports and windows and a fleet of ships, decide which ship carries which cargo and in what port sequence.
tasks.inputs: cargoes, ports, time windows, fleet, sailing times and costs
tasks.outputs: ship schedules and cargo assignments; profit
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: Hemmati et al. (2014) benchmark suite for industrial and tramp ship routing and scheduling

tasks.name: Berth and quay crane allocation
tasks.definition: Given arriving ships with handling volumes and windows, and a quay with cranes, assign berthing positions, times and cranes.
tasks.inputs: ship arrivals, lengths, workloads, quay layout, cranes
tasks.outputs: berth plan, crane assignments and schedules
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: Cordeau et al. (2005) berth allocation instances and the Meisel and Bierwirth quay crane scheduling set

tasks.name: Container stowage planning
tasks.definition: Given the containers to load at each port of a rotation and the ship's bay structure, assign slots that respect stability, strength, reefer and dangerous-goods rules and minimize restows.
tasks.inputs: container list with weights and destinations, vessel profile, rotation
tasks.outputs: bay plan and stowage message; stability and restow count
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: published instances exist from academic work but no widely adopted set

capabilities.name: Rail operations
capabilities.definition: Given the track network, trains, cars and crews, plan and control train movements, enforce safe operation and manage yards and car supply.

crosswalk.label: Railway infrastructure, rolling stock, timetable and interlocking schemas

onet_categories: Data base user interface and query software
Materials requirements planning logistics and supply chain software
capabilities.notes: Was seed 'Rail operations and yard management'. Passenger timetabling sits in public transit; car and wheel repair shops go to operate.

tasks.name: Train dispatching and meet-pass planning
tasks.definition: Given trains on a network with positions, priorities and sidings, decide meets, passes and movement authorities to minimize delay.
tasks.inputs: track layout, train positions and schedules, priorities, maintenance windows
tasks.outputs: movement plan with meets and passes; authorities issued
onet_products: Rail Traffic Track Warrant Control System
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: INFORMS Railway Applications Section competition instances exist for train dispatching

tasks.name: Train control enforcement
tasks.definition: Given a train's consist, position and speed and the track's limits and authorities, predict its braking curve and enforce stops and speed limits.
tasks.inputs: consist and braking data, track profile, speed restrictions, authorities, position
tasks.outputs: braking predictions, warnings, enforcement commands
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: braking curve models (ETCS braking curves) are specified and can be tested, but not ranked

tasks.name: Train running time calculation
tasks.definition: Given a train's consist and the line's gradients, curves and speed limits, compute the speed profile, running time and energy.
tasks.inputs: locomotive and car data, track profile, speed limits, stops
tasks.outputs: speed-distance profile, running time, energy use
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: physics is well defined and results can be checked against measured runs, without a shared set

tasks.name: Rail yard inventory and switching
tasks.definition: Given cars arriving, departing trains and equipment reads, track each car's location and build the switching and classification plan.
tasks.inputs: car inventory, equipment identification reads, train consists, yard tracks
tasks.outputs: car locations by track, switch lists, classification sequence
onet_products: Softrail AEI Automatic Yard Tracking System
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: hump yard sorting has published models and instances, but no shared benchmark

tasks.name: Freight car ordering and distribution
tasks.definition: Given customer car orders and empty car supply, allocate and route empty cars to loading points.
tasks.inputs: car orders, empty car locations, car types, transit times
tasks.outputs: car assignments and empty movements
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: formulated as a transportation problem; no public instances

tasks.name: Train crew assignment
tasks.definition: Given trains to operate, crew pools, rest rules and crew positions, assign crews to trains and plan deadheads.
tasks.inputs: train schedule, crew pools and positions, labor rules
tasks.outputs: crew assignments and deadheads; cost
onet_products: Freight Rail Crew Optimization Scheduling FRCOS software
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: set-covering formulations as in airline crew scheduling, without public rail instances

capabilities.name: Public transit planning and information
capabilities.definition: Given a city's travel demand, streets and operating resources, design transit routes and timetables, schedule vehicles and crews, and tell riders how and when to travel.

crosswalk.label: General Transit Feed Specification (Schedule and Realtime)

capabilities.notes: Was seed 'Public transit scheduling and passenger information'. O*NET lists almost no transit products, so task examples are empty; the capability is kept because its functions are distinct and well benchmarked. Paratransit routing is move.vehicle_routing.dial_a_ride.

tasks.name: Transit route network design
tasks.definition: Given a street network and an origin-destination demand matrix, choose a set of transit routes and frequencies that balances rider travel time and operating cost.
tasks.inputs: street network, demand matrix, fleet size, route constraints
tasks.outputs: route set and frequencies; rider and operator costs
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: Mandl's Swiss network and Mumford's instance set for transit route network design

tasks.name: Periodic timetabling
tasks.definition: Given lines, frequencies and transfer and headway requirements, set departure times that minimize passenger travel and waiting time.
tasks.inputs: lines, frequencies, running and dwell times, transfers, headway constraints
tasks.outputs: periodic timetable
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: PESPlib periodic event scheduling instances with best-known values

tasks.name: Transit vehicle scheduling
tasks.definition: Given timetabled trips and depots, chain trips into vehicle blocks that cover every trip with the fewest vehicles and least deadheading.
tasks.inputs: trips with times and terminals, depots, deadhead times, vehicle types
tasks.outputs: vehicle blocks; fleet size and deadhead cost
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: multiple-depot vehicle scheduling instance generators are published, but no fixed standard set

tasks.name: Transit crew scheduling
tasks.definition: Given vehicle blocks and labor rules, cut blocks into driver runs and assign runs to operators.
tasks.inputs: vehicle blocks, relief points, labor rules
tasks.outputs: runs and rosters; paid hours
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: set-covering formulations; few public instances

tasks.name: Transit journey planning
tasks.definition: Given a timetable, real-time updates and a traveler's origin, destination and time, find the fastest or Pareto-optimal itineraries including walking and transfers.
tasks.inputs: timetable feed, real-time updates, street network, query
tasks.outputs: itineraries with legs, times and transfers
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: public timetable feeds (London, Switzerland, Germany) with random query sets are the standard benchmark for RAPTOR-family algorithms

tasks.name: Real-time arrival prediction
tasks.definition: Given vehicle positions and the schedule, predict when each vehicle will reach each downstream stop.
tasks.inputs: vehicle positions, schedule, historical running times
tasks.outputs: predicted arrival times by stop
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: open vehicle-position archives allow scoring, but no shared split

capabilities.name: Travel reservation and distribution
capabilities.definition: Given carriers' schedules, fares and seat inventory, find, price, book and ticket travel, and set how much inventory to sell at each fare.
onet_categories: Data base user interface and query software
capabilities.notes: Was seed 'Travel reservation and distribution systems'. Restricted to carrier inventory, fares and distribution; hotel and restaurant reservations belong to commerce.

tasks.name: Availability and fare shopping
tasks.definition: Given an origin, destination and dates, search schedules, seat availability and fares to return priced itineraries.
tasks.inputs: schedules, availability, fares and rules, query
tasks.outputs: priced itinerary options
onet_products: Airline global distribution systems GDS software
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: fare construction is deterministic given filed fares and rules, which are licensed

tasks.name: Reservation and ticketing
tasks.definition: Given a chosen itinerary and passengers, hold seats in carrier inventory, create the passenger record and issue tickets and documents.
tasks.inputs: itinerary, passenger data, payment, inventory
tasks.outputs: passenger name record, tickets, seat assignments
onet_products: Sabre Airline Solutions SabreSonic Customer Sales & Service
tasks.benchmarkable: no: transactional

tasks.name: Seat inventory revenue management
tasks.definition: Given demand forecasts by fare class and itinerary, set booking limits or bid prices that maximize expected revenue.
tasks.inputs: demand forecasts by fare and itinerary, capacity, fares
tasks.outputs: booking limits or bid prices; expected revenue
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: textbook network revenue management instances exist (for example Topaloglu's), but no industry standard set

capabilities.name: Road navigation and traffic engineering
capabilities.definition: Given a road network, traffic and travel demand, find routes for drivers, and analyse, time and forecast traffic on the network.
capabilities.notes: Was seed 'Road navigation and traffic management'. Traffic engineering analysis and travel demand forecasting added here: they model how people and vehicles move on roads, and no other domain's boundary names them. Road geometric design stays with design.

tasks.name: Road shortest path routing
tasks.definition: Given a road graph with travel times and an origin and destination, compute the fastest route, possibly at continental scale and with live travel times.
tasks.inputs: road graph, edge travel times, origin, destination, departure time
tasks.outputs: route geometry, travel time and distance
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: the 9th DIMACS Implementation Challenge road networks are the standard shortest-path benchmark

tasks.name: Truck routing and mileage
tasks.definition: Given vehicle dimensions, weight and hazardous load, and a road network with legal restrictions, find a legal route and compute billing mileage by jurisdiction.
tasks.inputs: vehicle profile, origin, stops, restriction data
tasks.outputs: legal route, distance by state or country, tolls
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: legality is checkable against restriction data, which is mostly proprietary

tasks.name: Traffic signal timing optimization
tasks.definition: Given intersection geometry, turning volumes and phasing, compute cycle lengths, splits and offsets that minimize delay along a corridor or network.
tasks.inputs: intersection lanes, turning movement counts, phasing, pedestrian needs
tasks.outputs: signal timing plans; delay, stops and progression measures
onet_products: Texas Transportation Institute TTI Progression Analysis and Signal System Evaluation Routine PASSER
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: scored by delay in simulation; open scenario sets exist for reinforcement-learning signal control but none is standard

tasks.name: Highway and intersection capacity analysis
tasks.definition: Given a road facility's geometry, control and traffic volumes, compute capacity, delay and level of service by the Highway Capacity Manual or equivalent methods.
tasks.inputs: facility geometry, control, volumes, heavy vehicles, peak factors
tasks.outputs: capacity, delay, queue and level of service
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: the Highway Capacity Manual's example problems have published reference answers

tasks.name: Traffic microsimulation
tasks.definition: Given a road network, control and demand, simulate individual vehicles' movements to estimate travel times, queues and emissions.
tasks.inputs: network, signal control, origin-destination demand, driver behavior parameters
tasks.outputs: vehicle trajectories, travel times, queues, performance measures
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: calibration against the public NGSIM vehicle trajectory datasets is common, but there is no ranked benchmark

tasks.name: Road safety analysis
tasks.definition: Given crash records and road and traffic data, locate high-crash sites, diagnose patterns and predict crash frequency for alternatives.
tasks.inputs: crash records, road inventory, traffic volumes
tasks.outputs: hot-spot rankings, collision diagrams, predicted crash frequencies
state_of_art: FHWA Interactive Highway Safety Design Model
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: Highway Safety Manual predictive models give reference values for worked examples

tasks.name: Travel demand forecasting and assignment
tasks.definition: Given zones, land use, networks and behavior models, forecast trips by origin, destination and mode and assign them to the network to equilibrium.
tasks.inputs: zone data, highway and transit networks, behavior model parameters
tasks.outputs: trip tables, mode shares, link volumes and travel times
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: the Transportation Networks for Research repository (Sioux Falls, Chicago and others) has best-known equilibrium assignments

existing_function_map.note: Split. The applied problems are here: routing to move.vehicle_routing (and real-time dispatch to move.fleet_dispatch), inventory and supply-chain planning to move.supply_chain_planning, warehouse management to move.warehouse_inventory, transportation management and load planning to move.freight_transport. Mathematical programming solvers and modeling languages (CPLEX, LINDO, LINGO, AMPL, GAMS, MINOS, SNOPT, OPL) go to science's optimization capability; production scheduling, APS and shop-floor MRP (Preactor, Asprova, finite capacity scheduling) go to produce.

open_questions: Traffic engineering (signal timing, capacity, microsimulation) and travel demand forecasting are placed in move under 'road navigation and traffic'. They could instead sit in simulate as network analysis, like water and power networks; the boundary table names neither.
Drone mission planning is handed to earth per its seed, but uncrewed aircraft operations generally (not only survey) fit move.flight_operations. Decide whether to split by purpose.
Travel revenue management and fare shopping could be viewed as commerce pricing. They are kept here because carrier seat inventory is transport-specific.

Crew scheduling appears three times (airline, rail, transit) by mode. A single cross-modal 'crew scheduling' capability would be more function-pure, but the instance sets and labor rules differ by mode.

The 'Materials requirements planning logistics and supply chain software' category mixes shop-floor MRP with logistics; the boundary between move.supply_chain_planning.supply_master_planning (multi-site) and produce's MRP (single-site explosion) should be confirmed with produce.
Fourteen capabilities with 90 tasks is at the top of the brief's range; parcel and mail could merge back into freight transportation if fewer capabilities are wanted.
